title.narrative: Ethiopia Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Water Supply, Sanitation, and Hygiene Project (WaSH) is 'to increase access to improved water supply and sanitation services for residents in participating woredas/towns and communities in Ethiopia.' There are three components to the project, the first component being rural water supply, sanitation and hygiene. This component aims to improve access to water supply and sanitation services, and to promote improved hygiene in rural areas. The component will finance the following activities: (i) construction and rehabilitation of community water supply schemes in participating woredas and communities; and (ii) construction and rehabilitation of institutional water and sanitation facilities in schools and health facilities in participating woredas and communities. The second component is the urban water supply, sanitation and hygiene. This component aims to improve access to water supply and sanitation services in urban areas (small and medium towns), and to strengthen the capacity of WaSH officials to plan and manage these services in a sustainable manner. Finally, the third component is the project management monitoring and evaluation. This component aims to support and build the capacity of WaSH agencies at federal, regional, and local government levels to plan, implement, and manage water supply and sanitation services under their jurisdiction.
The proposed development objective of the project is to “increase access to improved water supply and sanitation services for residents in participating woredas/towns and communities in Ethiopia.”

title.narrative: Institutional WaSH facilities constructed/ rehabilitated in Schools and health facilities under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Exceeded the target (100.2%). The target was revised in the first restructuring when the project scope was increased.  </p>

title.narrative: Number of participating towns that have established water boards and have business plans

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved (85 percent). The target was revised in the first restructuring when the project scope was increased. 20 medium towns and 102 small towns have established water boards and prepared business plans.</p>

title.narrative: Improved latrines constructed under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Exceeded the target (195 percent). The target was revised in the first restructuring when the project scope was increased. The achieved results reflect the number of new household latrines constructed during the project period.</p>

title.narrative: Number of people in urban areas provided with access to Improved Water Sources under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved (83 percent). The target was revised twice, in the first restructuring (to 2,160,000) and the second restructuring (to 1,500,000, in June 2019) due to the reduction of geographical scope of the urban component.</p>

title.narrative: Number of trained WWT, WaSHCO/ Water Board members

comment.narrative: <p>Exceeded the target (2154 percent). The target was revised in the first restructuring when the project scope was increased.</p>

title.narrative: Improved community water points constructed or rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved (72 percent). The target was revised in the first restructuring when the project scope was increased. The achieved results were less than the target because the regional bureaus decided to work on fewer number of larger schemes with more beneficiaries, such as rural piping systems (RPSs), instead of small water supply schemes (with less beneficiaries) during the implementation.</p>

title.narrative: People trained to improve hygiene behavior/sanitation practices under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Mostly met (93 percent). The target was revised in the first restructuring when the project scope was increased.</p>

title.narrative: Number of people in rural areas provided with access to Improved Water Sources under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Exceeded the target (106%). The target was revised in the first restructuring (March 2015), when other DPs joined the OWNP-CWA and the project scope was increased.</p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to "improved sanitation facilities under the proj.

comment.narrative: <p>Exceeded the target (176%). The target was revised in the first restructuring, and it remained the same, despite the reduction of geographical scope for the urban component.</p>

title.narrative: Additional volume of water produced from improved source under the project ( in participating towns)

comment.narrative: <p>Exceeded the target (119%). The target was revised in the first restructuring when the project scope was increased.</p>

title.narrative: Number of water utilities that the project is supporting

comment.narrative: <p>Mostly achieved (95 percent). The target was revised twice in the first restructuring (to 144 utilities) and in the second restructuring). At the project closing, 20 medium towns and 124 small towns have received different capacity building support. As a result, 89 towns have established and are managed by water utilities.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved (89 percent). The target was revised in the first restructuring, and it remained the same, despite the reduction of geographical scope for the Urban component. </p>
